deviation: No Flow | Air inlet to cathode
causes: LCV-200 fails closed or is closed wrongly by SIC-400, or the air compressor trips
consequences: No O2/CO2 reaches the cathode and the cathode loses its cooling. Cell voltage collapses and cells can reverse under load. Local overheating damages the electrolyte matrix and seals, unreacted fuel builds up, and the stack may need replacing
safeguards: FIT-110 / FI-110 air flow indication; PIT-110 / PI-110 air pressure indication; VE-100 / VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm; TE-200 / TE-210 via TT-410 to SIC-400 stack temperature control; BPCS control of air flow and pressure
recommendations: Add a low-low air flow trip on FIT-110 that is independent of the BPCS and isolates fuel (LCV-100, LCV-300) and the DC load; Confirm the fail-safe position of LCV-200 on loss of signal or air

deviation: Less Flow | Air inlet to cathode
causes: LCV-200 partly closed or sticking, SIC-400 fault, or the air compressor or filter is degraded
consequences: Too little oxidant and cooling for the cathode. Stack temperature rises, hot spots form, electrolyte evaporates and corrosion speeds up. Stack life is shortened
safeguards: FIT-110 / FI-110; TE-200 / TE-210, TT-410, SIC-400; TE-310 / TI-310 cathode outlet temperature; VZA-100 low voltage alarm
recommendations: Add a high-high stack temperature trip, independent of TT-410/SIC-400, that reduces load and fuel

deviation: More Flow | Air inlet to cathode
causes: LCV-200 fails open, or SIC-400 output fails high
consequences: The stack is overcooled and the cathode temperature falls toward the carbonate freezing point. Thermal stress and partial solidification can crack the matrix, with loss of output power
recommendations: Add a low stack temperature alarm on TT-410 with the operator response defined

deviation: No Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
causes: LCV-100 fails closed, or the natural gas compressor or water pump trips
consequences: The anode is starved of fuel while current is still drawn. Cell voltage reverses, the Ni anode oxidises, and the electrodes are damaged permanently. The heat balance is also upset because endothermic reforming is lost
safeguards: FIT-100 / FI-100; PIT-100 / PI-100; VE-100 / VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm; IE-300 / II-300 / IR-300 current monitoring via IT-400 to SIC-400
recommendations: Add a low-low feed flow / low-low cell voltage trip that disconnects the DC load; Make sure the load is automatically reduced in proportion to available fuel flow

deviation: More Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
causes: LCV-100 fails open, or SIC-400 output fails high
consequences: Too much endothermic reforming cools the stack. Unconverted fuel and anode pressure increase, raising the anode-cathode differential pressure, which can lead to gas crossover and local combustion inside the stack
safeguards: FIT-100 / FI-100; TE-200 / TE-210, TT-410, SIC-400; TE-300 / TI-300 anode outlet temperature
recommendations: Install anode-cathode differential pressure measurement with alarm and trip

deviation: Part of Composition | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
causes: Water pump failure or low water flow gives a low steam-to-carbon ratio
consequences: Carbon deposits in the reformer and anode. The catalyst deactivates, flow paths block and pressure drop rises, causing performance loss and stack damage
safeguards: FIT-100 / FI-100 (total feed flow only); BPCS fuel flow control
recommendations: Measure water and natural gas flows separately, with a low steam-to-carbon ratio alarm and natural gas cut-off

deviation: As well as Composition | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
causes: Sulphur compounds or other contaminants in the natural gas, or impurities in the water
consequences: The reforming catalyst and Ni anode are poisoned. Reforming drops off, the heat balance is upset, and stack performance degrades over time
recommendations: Confirm upstream desulphurisation and water treatment, and set periodic feed quality analysis

deviation: More Flow | H2 BOG to anode
causes: LCV-300 fails open, or a BOG surge from the cargo tanks or BOG compressor
consequences: The anode overpressures and the anode-cathode differential pressure rises. H2 crosses through the matrix or seals into the cathode, causing local combustion and hot spots. H2 can leak externally, with a risk of fire or explosion in the fuel cell space
safeguards: FIT-120 / FI-120; PIT-120 / PI-120; TE-200 / TE-210, TT-410, SIC-400; PSV-160 relief to Vent Out
recommendations: Add a high H2 BOG flow / high anode pressure trip that closes an independent shutdown valve upstream of LCV-300; Install anode-cathode differential pressure monitoring

deviation: No Flow | H2 BOG to anode
causes: LCV-300 fails closed, or the BOG compressor trips
consequences: Fuel to the anode falls, so cell voltage drops and part of the stack may be starved of fuel. BOG pressure also builds up in the cargo system (outside this node)
safeguards: FIT-120 / FI-120; VZA-100 low voltage alarm; Feed via LCV-100 remains available
recommendations: Confirm the BOG handling alternative when the stack cannot accept BOG

deviation: Reverse Flow | H2 BOG / Feed inlet lines
causes: Supply pressure in the H2 BOG or feed line drops below stack pressure, for example on a compressor trip
consequences: Hot reformed gas (H2, CO) flows back into the upstream lines and compressors. This can overheat equipment, mix gas into another system, and expose people to toxic CO
recommendations: Install check valves on the feed and H2 BOG inlet lines; Close LCV-100 / LCV-300 on low supply pressure

deviation: More Temperature | MCFC stack
causes: Air/fuel heat balance is lost, SIC-400 fails, or TE-200/TE-210 reads low and the controller acts on the false reading
consequences: The stack runs above design temperature. Carbonate evaporates, corrosion speeds up, and seals and the matrix fail. The resulting H2/CO leak can ignite (fire), and CO is toxic
safeguards: TE-200 / TE-210 with TI-200 / TI-210; TT-410 / SIC-400; TE-300 / TI-300 and TE-310 / TI-310 exhaust temperatures
recommendations: Provide a SIL 1 high-high stack temperature trip from an independent sensor that isolates fuel and disconnects the load

deviation: Less Temperature | MCFC stack
causes: Excess air or feed flow, a sudden load reduction, or a temperature control fault
consequences: The electrolyte partly solidifies and the matrix cracks from thermal cycling. Gas crosses over on restart, and the stack is damaged permanently
recommendations: Add a low-low stack temperature alarm and a hot-standby procedure that keeps the stack above the electrolyte freezing point

deviation: More Pressure | Anode outlet
causes: BV-400 (fail closed) closes spuriously on loss of signal or actuator power, or the downstream line is blocked
consequences: Anode pressure rises while fuel is still supplied. High differential pressure across the electrolyte forces H2/CO into the cathode, causing combustion and hot spots. Seals can fail and release H2/CO externally (fire, explosion, CO toxicity)
safeguards: PSV-160 relief to Vent Out; TE-300 / TI-300; PIT-100 / PIT-120 upstream pressure indication
recommendations: Add an anode outlet pressure transmitter with a high alarm and a trip that closes LCV-100 / LCV-300; Interlock BV-400 closure with fuel isolation; Verify that PSV-160 protects the anode side and is sized for this case

deviation: More Pressure | Cathode outlet
causes: BV-410 (fail closed) closes spuriously, or the downstream line is blocked
consequences: The cathode overpressures and the differential pressure reverses, pushing air into the anode. Mixing O2 with fuel causes local combustion, damages the stack, and can break seals
safeguards: PSV-160 relief to Vent Out; BV-160 (fail open) vent valve; TE-310 / TI-310; PIT-110 / PI-110
recommendations: Interlock BV-410 closure with air flow reduction (LCV-200) and stack shutdown; Add a cathode outlet pressure measurement

deviation: More Flow | Vent Out (BV-160 / PSV-160)
causes: BV-160 (fail open) opens spuriously on loss of signal or utility, or PSV-160 lifts or passes
consequences: The stack depressurises suddenly and hot, possibly flammable gas is released at Vent Out. It may ignite at the vent outlet, and the pressure transient upsets the stack
safeguards: Vent routed to a dedicated Vent Out
recommendations: Confirm the vent outlet is in a safe location per class rules for hydrogen-fuelled ships, with a dispersion study; Add BV-160 position indication and an alarm

deviation: Less Pressure | MCFC stack (external leak)
causes: Wet-seal or flange leak at 650 °C, or carbonate corrosion of the stack housing or manifolds
consequences: H2, CO and natural gas are released into the fuel cell space. Fire or explosion is possible, people can be exposed to toxic CO, and propulsion power may be lost
safeguards: PIT-100 / PIT-110 / PIT-120 pressure indication; VZA-100 low voltage alarm
recommendations: Provide H2 and CO gas detection in the fuel cell space, interlocked to fuel isolation and ventilation; Enclose the stack with ventilation monitoring per IGF Code / class rules

deviation: More Power | DC-Power output
causes: Propulsion demand exceeds stack capacity, or current control fails
consequences: Fuel utilisation becomes too high and parts of the anode are starved. Cell voltage falls, cells can reverse, overheating follows, and the stack degrades
safeguards: IE-300 / II-300 / IR-300 current indication and recording; VE-100 / VZA-100 low voltage alarm; IT-400 to SIC-400
recommendations: Limit current in the power converter based on available fuel flow and the low-voltage threshold; Add battery or energy storage to buffer load transients

deviation: No Power | DC-Power output
causes: Sudden loss of load (propulsion trip, breaker opens), or a short circuit in the DC system
consequences: On open circuit the cell voltage rises and unconsumed fuel goes to Anode Out. Without the cell reaction heat the stack cools. A short circuit can cause arcing and damage to the electrical system, and propulsion is lost
safeguards: VE-110 / VZA-110 high voltage alarm; IE-300 / II-300 current monitoring; SIC-400 fuel and air control
recommendations: Cut fuel back automatically on load rejection; Confirm DC short-circuit protection and selectivity

deviation: No Utility | Instrument air / control power to BPCS and valves
causes: Loss of instrument air or UPS/control power
consequences: BV-400 and BV-410 fail closed and BV-160 fails open. If LCV-100/LCV-300 do not also fail closed, fuel keeps entering a blocked-in stack, overpressuring it and venting H2 at Vent Out
safeguards: BV-160 fail open to Vent Out; PSV-160
recommendations: Specify LCV-100 and LCV-300 as fail-closed and review the fail position of LCV-200 for a safe shutdown; Provide a UPS for the BPCS and safety system

deviation: Before Operation | Start-up sequence
causes: Feed or H2 BOG is admitted before the stack is purged and heated, or before air flow is established
consequences: A flammable mixture forms in the stack or vent and can explode. Feeding a cold reformer deposits carbon
safeguards: Operating procedures; TE-200 / TE-210 stack temperature indication
recommendations: Add start-up permissives: completed inert purge, minimum stack temperature, and confirmed air flow before LCV-100 / LCV-300 can open
